english.note: This is the all-purpose choice for something unclear, indistinct, or lacking a sharp outline.
Use this when an idea, memory, image, or impression is vague or unclear rather than physically dark.
Use this when something is hard to make out, or when speech, writing, or thinking is vague or poorly expressed.
Use this when dim means visually indistinct, hazy, or unclear.
Use this when a person's, thing's, or idea's character is vague or undefined rather than physically shapeless.
Use this for a memory, image, or idea that is vague rather than for atmospheric mist.
Use this for writing, images, or other visual details that are blurry or difficult to make out.

examples.english: This photo is too vague for me to make out clearly.
examples.traditional: 呢張相太模糊，我睇唔清楚。
